java: PSystemCommandFactory abandons a candidate as soon as a matched command executes with an error or no command matches the next line.
ClassDiagramFactory registers native class commands before CommandAllowMixing and before CommandCreateElementFull2(Mode.NORMAL_KEYWORD).
CommandCreateElementFull2 reuses state plus CommandCreateElementFull.ALL_TYPES and rejects Mode.NORMAL_KEYWORD unless allowmixing has already executed.
Pattern2.compileInternal compiles PlantUML command regexes with Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE, so uppercase spellings such as DATABASE, QUEUE, and BOUNDARY are valid inputs for the same command families.
rust: Commit 1b1b575c broadened the mixed-only family list from component-only to the full lowercase keyword set plus state.
The detection still compares trimmed.split_whitespace().next() directly against lowercase MIXED_ONLY_CLASS_KEYWORDS with no case normalization.
Quoted-container tie-breaking still relies on has_class_factory_decl, and lower-case native class controls such as entity and interface continue to set that flag.

findings.summary: The revised mechanism still does not model the full Java keyword family because Rust recognizes only lowercase spellings of mixed-only leaves.
details: Java command regexes are case-insensitive via Pattern2.compileInternal, so DATABASE, QUEUE, and BOUNDARY are valid spellings for the same CommandCreateElementFull2 family.
Rust compares the leading token literally against a lowercase MIXED_ONLY_CLASS_KEYWORDS slice and never normalizes case before that comparison.

Three fresh valid held-outs therefore route DESCRIPTION in Java but CLASS in Rust: checker_followup3_root_node_upper_database_lr, checker_followup3_nested_cloud_upper_queue_tb, and checker_followup3_upper_boundary_before_entity_tb.

findings.summary: The corrected account overstates the current implementation as a complete source-order model of the Java family.
details: The source-order behavior is still contingent on lowercase matching. A mixed-only leaf that appears before a later native class declaration should reject the class candidate regardless of case, but Rust misses uppercase BOUNDARY and keeps the class candidate viable until the later entity declaration wins the tie.

A preceding allowmixing does preserve CLASS selection for the uppercase boundary control, but Rust still drops the boundary element itself, leaving secondary executable residue even when dispatch matches.
